title: Dedupe size/measurement callbacks before calling setState to avoid phantom rerenders
answers: setPopoverMaxSize keeps triggering rerenders even though the size values are identical
Why does React update the DOM on every render even when no attributes visibly changed?
How to prevent a measurement/observer callback (ResizeObserver, floating-ui size middleware) from causing unnecessary rerenders
body: Symptom: calling a state setter with a newly-created object (e.g. `{width, height}`) on every measurement callback causes a rerender even when the numeric values are unchanged, and React's reconciliation then does attribute get/set work on elements like <input> with no visible change. Root cause: useComboboxFloat's `size()` middleware `apply` callback called `setPopoverMaxSize({width, height})` unconditionally on every floating-ui measurement, and object identity differs each time so React always rerenders. Fix pattern: keep a `useRef` mirror of the last applied value and compare primitive fields before calling the setter; only call `setPopoverMaxSize` when `width`/`height` actually changed, updating the ref first (see popoverMaxSizeRef in useComboboxFloat.ts). Constraints: use this when a callback-driven state update produces a fresh object/array each invocation but the consumer only cares about value equality, not for state that is genuinely expected to change every call.
applies: React state updates driven by external observers/middlewares (ResizeObserver, floating-ui size middleware, etc.) that may report unchanged values

search: Avoiding phantom rerenders from measurement callbacks: deduplicate state updates by keeping a useRef mirror of the last applied value and comparing primitive fields before calling setState. Root cause: callbacks (ResizeObserver, floating-ui size middleware) invoke state setters with fresh objects each time even when numeric values unchanged, triggering unnecessary rerenders. Fix pattern shown in packages/grafana-ui/src/components/Combobox/useComboboxFloat.ts (useComboboxFloat, size, popoverMaxSizeRef) checks value equality before calling setPopoverMaxSize. Constraint: use only when callback-driven updates produce fresh objects but consumer cares about value equality, not for state genuinely expected to change every call. Applies to React state driven by external observers/middlewares.
